questions.worked_solution:
Let $v=p+q\text{i},$ where $p,q\in {R}^{2},$ be an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =a+b\text{i}.$

Then, a complex solution of the system is given by

$$
{x}_{\text{complex}}(t)=v{e}^{\lambda t}.
$$

Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{complex}}(t) & =v{e}^{(a+b\text{i})t} \\  & ={e}^{at}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt))(p+q\text{i}) \\  & ={e}^{at}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)p-\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)q)+\text{i}{e}^{at}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)p+\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)q).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\text{x}(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{at}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)p-\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)q)+{c}_{2}{e}^{at}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)p+\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)q),
$$

where the parts $(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)p-\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)q)$ and $(\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)p+\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)q)$ are bounded.

Now, notice that the given curve is $\text{bounded}$ (and closed), representing $\text{an ellipse}$ that is traversed $\text{clockwise}.$

But we have that:

- ${e}^{at}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty $ when $a>0,$ and

- ${e}^{at}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty $ when $a<0.$

Thus, we must have $a=0.$

3.Identifying the Parameters of a System Given Its Phase Portrait?

The phase portrait for a system of linear differential equations whose matrix has two complex eigenvalues λ=a±bi is shown above. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

The given curve is
unbounded
unbounded
bounded
, representing
a spiral
a spiral
an ellipse
that is traversed
counterclockwise
counterclockwise
clockwise
. Thus, we must have
a≠0
a≠0
a=0
b=0
.

The spiral is traversed toward
infinity
infinity
the origin
as t→∞. Hence,
a>0
a>0
a<0
.
